notes: Comprehensive as of 2026-09-25. All 24 Departmentally Related Standing Committees (16 Lok Sabha-serviced, 8 Rajya Sabha-serviced) and the 3 Financial Committees (PAC, Estimates, COPU) have verified current chairs sourced live from prsindia.org's parliamentary-committees pages, cross-checked for the 8 Rajya Sabha DRSCs against Rajya Sabha's own committee-integration API (perfect match on all 8). Six Joint Parliamentary Committees on specific bills (One Nation One Election / 129th Amendment, 130th Amendment on removal of arrested ministers, Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, Corporate Laws Amendment 2026, FCRA Amendment 2026, and the now-concluded Waqf Amendment 2024) are included with status and, where available, chair — sourced from PRS Legislative Research bill-track pages and Wikipedia. GAPS: (1) For most 'other' Lok Sabha standing/administrative committees (Privileges, Ethics, Government Assurances, Petitions, Subordinate Legislation, Papers Laid, House Committee, Absence of Members, Private Members' Bills, MPLADS) the current (18th Lok Sabha (2024-2029 term, so far in its 2024-26 span)) chairperson could NOT be confirmed from any 2025-2026 dated source reachable with the available tools (WebSearch budget was exhausted session-wide before this segment started; Wikipedia's only relevant table is explicitly dated to the 17th Lok Sabha, 2019-2024, and its names were deliberately NOT carried forward as current to avoid presenting stale office-holders as live data). The committees themselves, their function and composition rules are included and high-confidence; only the 'holder' is missing. (2) For several Rajya Sabha 'other' committees (Business Advisory, Rules, General Purposes, House, MPLADS, ICT Management) Rajya Sabha's own official committee-integration API returned two different chair names across two of its endpoints (GetCommitteeChairman vs GetMastercommittee?catid=1); both names are recorded with a low-confidence flag rather than picking one arbitrarily. (3) Corporate Laws Amendment Bill 2026 JPC and FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 JPC chairs could not be confirmed from any source found. (4) The 5 Joint standing committees (Empowerment of Women, Welfare of SC/ST, Library, Offices of Profit, MP Salaries & Allowances) likewise have unconfirmed current chairs. (5) Public Accounts and Public Undertakings Committees are cross-cutting (examine CAG reports / CPSEs across all ministries) so no 'oversees' relations to specific ministries were added for them; Estimates Committee's 22 'oversees' relations instead reflect its ROTATING current-cycle (2026-27) examination group — the Committee has no fixed jurisdiction and selects a different set of ministries/schemes each year, so these relations should not be read as permanent. (6) Select Committees on specific 2025 bills (Income-Tax Bill 2025, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code Amendment 2025, Jan Vishwas Amendment 2025) exist per sansad.in's committee registry but were not researched in depth (out of core scope; flagged for potential follow-up). (7) DPIIT (Dept for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) does not appear explicitly under any DRSC's examined-ministries list in the source data gathered; likely falls under the Commerce DRSC in practice but this was not independently confirmed.

entities.name: Joint Committee on the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024
aliases: JPC on One Nation One Election
entities.description: Examines the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, which together propose to hold simultaneous ('one nation, one election') elections to the Lok Sabha and all State Legislative Assemblies. Introduced in Lok Sabha 17 December 2024 and referred to this JPC on 19 December 2024; enlarged to 39 members (27 Lok Sabha + 12 Rajya Sabha) after cross-party demands. As of September 2026 the JPC is still consulting stakeholders (including state Chief Ministers) and has not yet presented its report; chairman P. P. Chaudhary has indicated it is examining feasibility for the 2029 general elections.
entities.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

entities.name: Joint Committee on the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2025, and the Government of Union Territories (Amendment) Bill, 2025
aliases: JPC on Removal of Arrested Ministers
entities.description: Examines bills that would provide for the automatic removal of a Prime Minister, Chief Minister or other Minister (including in Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir) who is arrested and held in custody for 30 consecutive days on a serious criminal charge. Introduced in Lok Sabha on 20 August 2025 and referred to this JPC the same day. As of September 2026 the bills remain with the JPC; no report has been presented.
entities.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

entities.name: Joint Committee on the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025
entities.description: Examines the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025, which replaces the UGC, AICTE and NCTE with a single higher-education regulatory Commission. Introduced in Lok Sabha on 15 December 2025 and referred to this JPC on 16 December 2025. As of September 2026 the bill remains in committee; no report has been presented.
entities.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

entities.name: Joint Committee on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
entities.description: Examined the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which amends the Companies Act, 2013 and the LLP Act, 2008 (decriminalisation of offences, civil penalties). Introduced in Lok Sabha 23 March 2026 and referred to this JPC the same day; the JPC presented its report on 3 August 2026. Chairperson not independently confirmed from a public source as of research date.
entities.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

entities.name: Joint Committee on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026
entities.description: Examines the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which creates a framework for supervision, management and disposal of foreign contributions/assets of organisations that cease to hold an FCRA certificate. Introduced in Lok Sabha 25 March 2026; referred to this JPC (per PRS bill-track status) 12 August 2026. As of September 2026 the bill remains in committee. Chairperson not independently confirmed from a public source as of research date.
entities.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

entities.name: Joint Committee on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024
entities.description: Examined the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024. Introduced in Lok Sabha 8 August 2024 and referred to this JPC the same day; the JPC presented its report on 30 January 2025. The Bill (incorporating the JPC's recommendations) was passed by Lok Sabha on 2 April 2025 and by Rajya Sabha on 3 April 2025, enacted as the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025. The JPC's mandate is concluded; it is not active as of September 2026.
entities.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

top-level notes: '18th Lok Sabha, 2024-26 term' -> '18th Lok Sabha (2024-2029 term, so far in its 2024-26 span)' (18th LS's constitutional term runs to 2029, not 2026; avoids implying the House itself expires in 2026)

Added holder.wikipedia for 44 positions (schema requires this field 'when a page exists'; 0 of 46 named holders had it before verification). Each URL was checked live via curl (HTTP 200) and cross-checked against the person's infobox to rule out same-name collisions (e.g. rejected en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Jha_(politician) — a Congress spokesperson from Bhagalpur, Bihar — as a false match for DRSC Transport/Tourism/Culture chair Sanjay Kumar Jha, a JD(U) Rajya Sabha MP from Bihar since 2024-04-04; used Sanjay_Kumar_Jha instead). Could not find a Wikipedia page for 'Azad Kirti Jha' (TMC, DRSC Chemicals & Fertilizers chair, Bardhaman-Durgapur, per PRS profile prsindia.org/mptrack/18-lok-sabha/azad-kirti-jha) — left without a wikipedia URL rather than guessing.
